United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: Entrepreneurship Empowering young men, girls and students to participate in entrepreneurship using communications and information technology in the modern era, and to contribute to achieving sustainable development goals.

description.narrative:
Introduction The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) gives great attention to building a society of knowledge and information, inclusive of all, to achieve sustainable development, innovation and leadership in the use of communication and information technology for the purposes of education and entrepreneurship, and ensuring that everyone’s equal participation in the development of society is an essential factor in achieving:  The fourth goal of sustainable development, which is related to the quality of education,  The fifth goal, which considers gender equality,  The ninth goal, which relates to industry and innovation; by strengthening industry and innovation, new economic opportunities can be provided, and increase and speed of access to sources of information and technology can be available, which enhances economic development and contributes to protection of fundamental freedoms.  The tenth goal, which relates to alleviating gaps in societies and between countries,  The seventeenth goal, which relates to partnerships to achieve the goals.
This aims to enhance international cooperation and partnerships between the public and private sectors and civil society, to achieve the goals of sustainable development, including the protection of freedoms, and providing access to information for all. This is to enhance the capabilities of young people, achieve the principle of universal access to information, and provide opportunities for comprehensive, equitable quality education and lifelong learning for all, and for the different marginalized and vulnerable groups (women, girls, youth, and people with special needs). The progress achieved in the field of communications and information technology and the increasing interconnectedness between the societies of knowledge will enhance work to advance innovation, entrepreneurship, renovation, and creating new job opportunities for youth, women, and girls to improve the standard of their living and income. Open resources programs of information and technology provide the opportunity to support and empower developing countries and all individuals and society. They also ensures social and economic inclusion for all, which contributes to achieving sustainable development goals and reducing the percentage of young people deprived of jobs, education or training opportunities. The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) has a major role in enhancing the effective contribution of women and girls in the field of using communication and information technology in the fields of education, science and culture. Due to people’s increasing reliance on digital technological means, the use of social media creates opportunities of work for young people, and at the same time creates great challenges. Opportunities that can be seized in this regard include social learning, innovation, knowledge exchange, democratic participation, and intercultural dialogue. One of the most important challenges that must be addressed is the spread of misinformation and widespread disinformation, which directly affects young people as the main users of the internet and social media globally. Through this project, the Egyptian National Committee, as a link between the UNESCO and the concerned parties, will contribute to building an inclusive society of knowledge and information to achieve sustainable development by creating a specialized training package in entrepreneurship and making good use of modern technology and artificial intelligence tools to qualify young people for the labor market and increase their capabilities for compete globally. Through this project, the Egyptian National Committee will provide partnerships and cooperation between:
1. Educational institutions and teachers who play an essential role in enhancing media and information literacy among learners and enabling them to acquire the necessary competencies to participate in the digital field as global citizens. It will take place at all levels of primary and secondary education, as well as in the field of adult learning. 2. Youth organizations, young people and especially young women; young people are the most active users of digital technologies, therefore it is necessary to ensure that they acquire the necessary digital competencies in the field of media and information literacy, and to ensure their ability to have effective entrepreneurship that enables them to create the desired impact to face the challenges related to the development of this field. So, the necessary measures will be taken to achieve the following: • Enabling young people to acquire competencies in the field of media, information literacy and digital competencies and using them as peer educators • Enhancing the capacity of youth-led organizations to integrate media and information literacy into their activities, policies and strategies through means that include encouraging intercultural dialogue to achieve understanding; • Supporting effective youth actions that enable young people to find the necessary solutions and play an active role as they are able to bring about the desired change in order to achieve social inclusion and combat all forms of exclusion, racism and discrimination in the digital field; • Assuring that young people’s use of digital technologies, and the impact of these means on them is part and parcel of comprehensive youth development approaches in youth policies; • Enhancing science-based youth organizations to have the desired impact in decision-making processes; • Relying on advances and developments in the field of neurotechnology to find solutions to serious mental health problems.
3. Media institutions and media workers; by establishing partnerships with digital communications platforms as principal actors to integrate media and information literacy in digital spaces. Working with the above-mentioned groups, the necessary links will be created between them to put relevant tools on digital learning and guidelines on digital citizenship into practice. This is to cope with UNESCO’s endeavors to take gender equality into account as one of its main areas of focus, while recognizing the digital gap that exists between men and women, which prevents women and girls from benefiting from digital technology and participating in the digital field through engaging men and boys as responsible allies to advance gender equality in the digital sphere. “71% of young people worldwide are connected to the Internet, compared to 57% of the total population.” International Telecommunication Union.
